title: Effect of Sintering Temperature on the Microstructure and Integrated Properties of MgAlTiVFeCo Lightweight High-Entropy Alloy

recollection.starting_material: A mixture of elemental powders of Mg, Al, Ti, V, Fe, and Co in equiatomic or near-equiatomic ratios (guess)
recollection.intervention: Powder metallurgy processing followed by sintering at various temperatures (guess)
recollection.structure: A lightweight high-entropy alloy with a microstructure likely consisting of a solid solution phase (BCC/FCC) and potentially secondary phases, with grain size varying by sintering temperature (guess)
recollection.mechanism: Sintering temperature controls diffusion rates, grain growth, and phase formation, thereby influencing density, mechanical strength, and corrosion resistance (guess)
recollection.results: Optimal sintering temperature likely yields a balance of high density, improved mechanical properties (hardness, compressive strength), and low density, with specific quantitative values for density and strength being temperature-dependent (guess)

score.note: The recollection only generically identifies temperature-varied powder sintering, without SPS or the 1000 °C optimum. It speculates about solid-solution/secondary phases but misses the dense microstructure and specific oxide barrier phases. The diffusion-based mechanism is broadly plausible but omits passive-film formation, chloride blocking, and parabolic biphasic oxidation. No quantitative results are recalled.
